statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is strictly increasing (for every p with 0 <= p and p + 1 < len(r), r[p] < r[p + 1]), and for every integer x, x occurs in r (there exists p with 0 <= p < len(r) and r[p] = x) if and only if 100 <= x <= 999, x mod 2 = 0, and there exist pairwise distinct indices i, j, k with 0 <= i < len(digits), 0 <= j < len(digits), 0 <= k < len(digits) such that digits[i] = x / 100, digits[j] = (x / 10) mod 10, and digits[k] = x mod 10.
preconditions: len(digits) >= 3 and len(digits) <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(digits), 0 <= digits[i] <= 9.

statement: Whenever the input satisfies the preconditions, the function returns a result r; in particular it does not fail because of arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or a panic.
